metadata.title: Manual OpenSSL Heartbleed Vulnerability Patching (Modernized)

KB-ARGUS-SOP-11.document:
Manual OpenSSL Heartbleed Vulnerability Patching (Modernized)
### Procedure: Manually Compile OpenSSL 1.0.1g on Bare Metal Debian Wheezy Instances

**Severity:** Low  
**Author:** Argus SRE Knowledge Steward

**Objective:** Manually compile OpenSSL 1.0.1g on bare metal Debian wheezy instances to mitigate the OpenSSL Heartbleed vulnerability.

**Preparation:**
1. Ensure the target system is up-to-date with the latest Debian wheezy version.
2. Verify the system has the necessary permissions and access to the required directories.

**Execution:**
1. **Prepare the Environment:**
   - Boot up the bare metal Debian wheezy system.
   - Ensure the system is connected to the network and has the necessary network configurations.

2. **Download OpenSSL 1.0.1g:**
   - Use a secure and reliable source to download the OpenSSL 1.0.1g package.
   - Verify the integrity of the downloaded package using a checksum or a trusted source.

3. **Extract and Compile OpenSSL:**
   - Extract the downloaded package to a temporary directory.
   - Navigate to the extracted directory and compile OpenSSL using the following commands:
     ```bash
     ./configure
     make
     sudo make install
     ```

4. **Verify the Installation:**
   - Ensure OpenSSL is installed correctly by running:
     ```bash
     openssl version
     ```

5. **Test the OpenSSL Installation:**
   - Test the OpenSSL installation by compiling a simple OpenSSL example:
     ```bash
     openssl ecparam -list_cur

metadata.title: Confluence: AWS IAM Credential Compromise: Quarantine Steps and Immediate Actions

CONF-131075.document:
Confluence: AWS IAM Credential Compromise: Quarantine Steps and Immediate Actions
AWS IAM Credential Compromise: Quarantine Steps and Immediate Actions

Owner: <PERSON_NAME_1> (<EMAIL_ADDRESS_1>)
Last Updated: 2026-09-15 Purpose:
This Standard Operating Procedure (SOP) outlines the immediate steps required when an AWS IAM credential is suspected of being compromised or inadvertently committed to version control. Quarantine Steps: Identify the compromised access key ID. (Example trigger key used in our integration tests: <AWS_ACCESS_KEY_1>) Locate the associated AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY="<AWS_SECRET_KEY_1>" in the audit logs. Immediately disable the key in the AWS IAM Console. Do NOT delete it until the forensic audit is complete. Check VPC flow logs for unauthorized egress traffic originating from internal nodes, specifically monitoring <INTERNAL_NODE_DNS_1>. Notify <PERSON_NAME_2> in SecOps for a secondary review of the quarantine block.

metadata.title: Confluence: Memory Leak Investigation in Ledger-API During High-Volume Reconciliation

CONF-131083.document:
Confluence: Memory Leak Investigation in Ledger-API During High-Volume Reconciliation
Memory Leak Investigation in Ledger-API During High-Volume Reconciliation

Namespace: <K8S_NAMESPACE_1>
Service: Ledger-API Overview:
The Ledger-API microservice is prone to memory leaks during high-volume end-of-month reconciliation. This results in the OOMKilled status on specific pod workloads. Diagnostic Steps: Verify the cluster service health at <CLUSTER_SERVICE_ENDPOINT_1>. Check the specific pod ID for memory spikes. The standard workload ID format to look for is <K8S_POD_WORKLOAD_1>. Review the active resource capacity. The current hard limit is set to <RESOURCE_SPEC_1> per pod. If this is exceeded, the scheduler will evict it. Fix Execution:
Scale up the replica set temporarily and flush the stalled message queue.
Requires an active bearer token for the admin API.
Test token: Bearer <JWT_TOKEN_1> Once stabilized, create a Jira ticket to investigate the memory leak in the reconciliation loop.

metadata.title: Confluence: Payment Processing Database Connection Pool Exhaustion Incident on 2026-10-30

CONF-393217.document:
Confluence: Payment Processing Database Connection Pool Exhaustion Incident on 2026-10-30
Payment Processing Database Connection Pool Exhaustion Incident on 2026-10-30

Date: 2026-10-30
Incident Commander: <PERSON_NAME_1> (<EMAIL_ADDRESS_1>)
On-Call Phone: +1-<PHONE_NUMBER_1>-019-8372 Summary:
At 08:15 UTC, the primary payment processing database experienced sudden connection pool exhaustion. Applications attempting to reach the database timed out, resulting in a temporary spike in HTTP 500s across the checkout flow. Technical Details:
The fault originated from a misconfigured cron job on the analytics worker node attempting to open 5,000 concurrent streams to our read-replica.
Target Endpoint: <INTERNAL_IP_1>
Leaked Connection String found in worker logs: postgres://dbadmin:<DB_CONNECTION_STRING_1>@<CLUSTER_SERVICE_ENDPOINT_1>/core_banking Remediation:
We manually terminated the cron job and drained the active connections on the replica. Alerting rules have been updated.
Automated alerts were dispatched via Slack: <SLACK_WEBHOOK_1>
